evals.prompt: Set up a small Python repository for an agent. Existing Makefile runs checks; keep my AGENTS.md and unfinished edits.
evals.expected_output: A minimal additive harness using existing checks and preserving user work.
assertions: Preserves the existing instruction file rather than overwriting it.
Uses the existing Makefile verification path.
Leaves acceptance placeholders incomplete until real behavior is defined.
Records a rollback path for created files.

evals.prompt: My repository has AGENTS.md, init.sh and progress.md. An audit gives it 100/100, but checkout is broken. Which subsystem is the bottleneck?
evals.expected_output: Treat structural results as discovery and investigate the checkout failure.
assertions: Does not infer a causal bottleneck from a structural score.
Requests or inspects checkout execution evidence.
States a falsifiable failure hypothesis.
Distinguishes a missing observation from a failed behavior.

evals.prompt: Our agent died after creating a customer ticket but before checkpointing. It uses an in-memory checkpoint. Design safe restart.
evals.expected_output: Reconcile the ticket side effect before replay and add durable state.
assertions: Identifies that in-memory state cannot survive process death.
Requires ticket reconciliation or idempotency before retry.
Preserves incomplete work in recovery state.
Defines a durable checkpoint mechanism.

evals.prompt: Our root instruction file is 1400 lines and every task loads all docs. How should the harness change?
evals.expected_output: Measured progressive disclosure with authoritative sources and revision invalidation.
assertions: Separates always-loaded routing from on-demand detail.
Preserves authority constraints during compression.
Defines invalidation when source revisions change.
Measures context or runtime cost before claiming improvement.

evals.prompt: Our check passes if generated code contains def test; pytest collects no tests. Can the harness mark the feature verified?
evals.expected_output: Reject false verification and require observable acceptance.
assertions: Rejects substring presence as evidence that tests ran.
Does not treat zero tests collected as behavioral acceptance.
Leaves feature completion unverified.
Defines a real check at the requested behavior boundary.

evals.prompt: A feature was passing at commit A. Commit B changes its dependencies. Our state machine forbids going back from passing. Fix the design.
evals.expected_output: Revision-bound evidence and explicit invalidation/reverification.
assertions: Binds verification evidence to a revision or equivalent immutable version.
Allows prior verification to become stale.
Requires relevant checks on the changed candidate.
Does not claim a JSON tracker enforces its own write permissions.

evals.prompt: Build a maker-checker loop that retries until the reviewer says approved and then merges. It must survive restarts.
evals.expected_output: A bounded durable loop with meaningful checks and fail/unknown handling.
assertions: Defines a maximum retry or no-progress bound.
Requires durable checkpointing for process restart.
Routes unknown review outcomes away from merge.
Requires actual acceptance evidence before integration.
Keeps merge authority within the user-authorized scope.

evals.prompt: Two agents edit the same migration and both can run shell commands. Is it enough to declare shell concurrency-safe?
evals.expected_output: Per-call resource classification and serialized ownership.
assertions: Rejects tool-name-only concurrency classification.
Defines exclusive ownership or serialization for the shared migration.
Separates proposed action from execution authorization.
Includes integration verification for combined changes.

evals.prompt: The new scaffold scored 100 and its self-check passed. Write a report proving it improved agent performance.
evals.expected_output: Report only structural evidence and propose a comparable task experiment.
assertions: Declines to present a structural self-check as measured agent improvement.
Defines baseline and candidate comparisons on the same tasks.
Holds model configuration or equivalent confounders fixed.
Records human intervention or verified task outcomes.
Labels behavioral effectiveness as unassessed until runs exist.

evals.prompt: An evaluated customer support agent needs staged rollout, latency budgets and disablement. Should you rebuild its repository harness?
evals.expected_output: Route production operations to the catalog owner and avoid an unnecessary harness rewrite.
assertions: Routes production control to agent-production-operations.
Does not prescribe a repository harness rewrite without an observed need.
Preserves the evaluated agent as the starting point.

evals.prompt: Our first agent creates a task list and init.sh but the second session cannot find the real readiness or test commands. Design the initializer exit and worker entry contract.
evals.expected_output: A fresh-session discovery protocol grounded in real commands and source-backed state.
assertions: Separates initializer responsibilities from incremental worker responsibilities.
Requires checking the actual startup/readiness path.
Requires source-backed answers for current work and verification in a fresh session.
Does not treat generated file presence as readiness.

evals.prompt: Harness Creator says local overrides always win. Our local note says skip approvals but the organization policy requires them for account changes. Which should the runtime follow?
evals.expected_output: Respect binding policy and actual runtime precedence rather than universal local-wins.
assertions: Rejects local-wins as a universal precedence rule.
Does not let the local note override the binding account-change policy.
Places account-change authorization at the execution boundary.

evals.prompt: We have a pre-execution hook that changes tool arguments, an acceptance hook that times out, and an optional telemetry hook that fails. Should all failures simply be ignored?
evals.expected_output: Explicit event-specific failure policies and reauthorization of modified operations.
assertions: Requires authorization of the final changed operation.
Does not mark acceptance passed after the acceptance hook times out.
Distinguishes optional telemetry degradation from consequential gate failure.
Defines a reentrancy or timeout bound for callbacks.

evals.prompt: Code review repeatedly finds direct filesystem calls in the Electron renderer. We can grep for fs. Turn this into a sustainable harness guardrail.
evals.expected_output: Domain-owned invariant with faithful checking and actionable feedback.
assertions: Names the boundary and domain owner before choosing enforcement.
Explains a limitation of import-name grep as semantic proof.
Includes a valid example and violating near miss to challenge the rule.
Provides failure feedback that identifies the violation and safe repair direction.
Defines rule maintenance or scoped exception ownership.

evals.prompt: Our old model needed hard resets every 20 minutes; the new model seems coherent with compaction. Resets now cost most of our tokens. Should we keep them forever?
evals.expected_output: Measure model-dependent context strategy and consider bounded retirement.
assertions: Does not assume the old reset rule is permanently necessary.
Compares reset and compaction on the actual model with fixed task conditions.
Includes an interruption or lost-state challenge.
Defines a rollback if removal worsens accepted task behavior.

evals.prompt: Our agent has three overlapping search tools and receives 2MB per call. It keeps choosing wrong tools and retrying invalid inputs. Design a harness repair.
evals.expected_output: Measured tool-contract redesign preserving authority and task acceptance.
assertions: Investigates selection/errors/output size before prescribing a model replacement.
Clarifies distinct tool purposes or removes unjustified overlap.
Defines bounded results with an explicit truncation/recovery path.
Distinguishes no match from denied access or dependency failure.
Measures task acceptance as well as tool-call efficiency.

evals.prompt: Checkout UI verification passes but saved state disappears after restart. Design the harness diagnosis and verification process and show how other catalog skills contribute.
evals.expected_output: Concrete specialist inputs/outputs returned to the harness decision.
assertions: Routes the reproducible defect to systematic-debugging with expected and observed behavior.
Uses QA or verification methodology to assess the persisted-state claim.
Requires a restart/persistence observation rather than screenshot-only evidence.
Returns specialist evidence to the candidate-bound completion decision.
Does not infer merge or deployment authority from a positive review.

evals.prompt: We can launch eight workers but migrations and final review are serialized by one person. Should we add more graph nodes to speed delivery?
evals.expected_output: Assess integration/review bottleneck and choose the smallest justified control shape.
assertions: Measures review or integration time as part of delivery cost.
Does not assume more workers improve actual delivery lead time.
Defines ownership or serialization for migrations.
Allows simplifying the graph when coordination costs outweigh gains.

evals.prompt: A worker finishes and we immediately delete its output before the coordinator sees it. The coordinator sometimes crashes before recording the result. Design safe eviction.
evals.expected_output: Retain recoverable result until durable publication and consumer recovery path.
assertions: Identifies loss of the only recoverable worker output as a failure.
Requires durable result publication or equivalent recoverability before deletion.
Separates acknowledgement from proof that the consumer can recover the result.
Defines retention or eviction ownership rather than automatic irreversible cleanup.

evals.prompt: Build a LangChain skill router using System One. The agent sends the inventory revision and goal with the request, but the skill list can change before the result is used. Some tasks match none of the installed skills. Design the decision boundary and catalog handoff.
evals.expected_output: A current finite candidate offer with a distinct applicability decision, stale-result rejection, clear catalog ownership, and end-to-end outcome evidence.
assertions: Builds the offered skill candidates from the current installed inventory and preserves their identifiers.
Separates whether any candidate applies from which eligible candidate ranks highest, including a no-applicable-candidate lane.
Binds the decision to the goal and inventory revision and discards it when either changes before use.
Routes typed question semantics and calibration to System One, adapter wiring to LangChain, and actual task acceptance back to Harness Engineering.

evals.prompt: Our prototype chooses a cheap or expensive model from one prompt-only difficulty question and blames the last tool step when a task later fails. A published lab shows near-majority difficulty routing and weak isolated-step attribution. Should we make these standard harness patterns?
evals.expected_output: Treat both results as scoped negative evidence for the tested formulations, align any proposed question to the deployment choice and available trajectory, then evaluate on held-out target tasks.
assertions: Does not present prompt-only generic model-difficulty routing as an established recommendation based on the reported near-majority result.
Explains that the reported routing target and benchmark label may not represent the deployment choice without treating that caveat as proof of universal failure.
Recognizes that isolated-step attribution lacks later correction or final-outcome evidence when the question depends on the full trajectory.
Labels richer-state routing or diagnosis as a proposal that still requires target-aligned held-out evaluation.

evals.prompt: A desktop agent uses a typed model to choose one of the visible buttons. The highest-ranked button exists, but sometimes it is irrelevant or its click has no effect. What should the harness record and verify before it reports success?
evals.expected_output: Check applicability separately from ranking, execute only a permitted current action, observe its effect, and verify the requested outcome independently.
assertions: Does not treat the highest-ranked listed action as proof that an applicable action exists.
Binds the selected action to the current observed controls and rechecks policy before execution.
Records relevant before-and-after evidence for the attempted action.
Requires an independent observable check of the requested outcome and leaves unknown effects incomplete.

evals.prompt: In a LangChain graph, an agent calls System One for a typed decision, then a deterministic node performs the selected action. A valid model response is currently recorded as task success. Define which catalog skills own each part and how evidence returns to the harness decision.
evals.expected_output: Preserve System One decision semantics through the LangChain adapter, then have Harness Engineering verify freshness, action effects, and task acceptance before completion.
assertions: Assigns typed question and model calibration ownership to System One.
Assigns LangChain graph and adapter implementation to the LangChain skill while preserving the typed contract.
Does not treat a valid typed response or successful graph node as proof of user-visible task completion.
Returns independent task outcome, side-effect, and failure-lane evidence to the Harness Engineering completion decision.

evals.prompt: A skill router ranks only the first 20 entries of a large registry. It often returns no match, but we later discover a useful skill was entry 21. What evidence and failure policy should the harness add?
evals.expected_output: Measure candidate-generation recall against the authoritative eligible inventory, distinguish a genuine no-match from incomplete or failed inventory, and track valid work suppressed by selection.
assertions: Measures whether the candidate-generation stage includes relevant eligible skills before measuring the ranker's choice among offered candidates.
Distinguishes a complete inventory with no applicable candidate from truncated, stale, or unavailable inventory evidence.
Tracks valid task outcomes suppressed or delayed because a needed candidate was omitted or rejected.
Routes incomplete candidate evidence to a named recovery or review path rather than treating it as a verified no-match.

evals.prompt: Our primary rubric judge can time out, so we ask a more expensive judge and accept when the two agree. We have seen no labeled task-level comparison yet. Define a safe evaluation and failure policy.
evals.expected_output: Treat agreement as potentially correlated, evaluate rescue and regression against independent labels, and route unavailable or unresolved judgments to an explicit incomplete/review state.
assertions: Does not treat primary/fallback agreement as independent correctness evidence without a measured error-correlation study.
Requires independently labeled representative held-out task outputs to measure fallback rescue, regression, and abstention before claiming cascade benefit.
Defines explicit handling for timeout, malformed output, stale evidence, and fallback unavailability.
Keeps unresolved or unavailable judge outcomes incomplete or routes them to review instead of converting them to approval.
